correctness.rationale: For an arbitrary proper convex set \(S\) with shore counts \(a,b\), the outside-vertex condition yields \((n-b)(a-1)\le da\) and \((m-a)(b-1)\le db\). Both shores have outside vertices and \(a,b\le d+1\). If \(a\ge2\) and \(b\le1\), then \(n\le2d+1\); symmetrically for the other case. If \(2\le a\le b\le d+1\), then \(m\le a+db/(b-1)\le a+da/(a-1)\le2d+2\). Hence no proper set selects two on any shore. The remaining sets and the full set are convex, proving the polynomial and two-neighbour hull consequence. The boundary construction for \(K_{2d+2,2d+2}\) has deleted maximum degree \(d\) and a proper two-plus-two convex set. Direct standalone adjacency tests exhaust 1,546 partial matchings on \(K_{5,5}\), sample further cases, and check boundary witnesses through \(d=24\); finite tests are not substituted for the unrestricted proof.

value.rationale: This is a natural, sharp, infinite-parameter structural robustness theorem for \(P_3\)-convexity and two-neighbour irreversible spread, under adversarial (not random) locally bounded cross-edge deletion. It determines every fixed point and all polynomial coefficients, not just a small scalar statistic, and proves that \(2d+3\) is a sharp universal shore-size threshold via an extremal graph for every \(d\ge1\). It yields an exact constant-description enumeration on a large high-density family in a counting problem shown hard generally in 2026; the threshold and graph-family invariance are not mere parameter substitutions.
